overview: The Board of Veterans' Appeals is the part of the Department of Veterans Affairs that decides appeals when veterans disagree with decisions on their benefits claims. This bill would require the board's yearly report to explain what caused appeals under the current appeals system to go undecided past the board's timeliness requirements, and what caused cases to be sent back (remanded) for more work, with the number and share of cases affected by each cause. It would also require the board to post online each week the docket dates of cases assigned to judges for a decision that week, noting that an assignment does not guarantee a decision that week. Cases that were moved up in line or sent back by the U.S. Court of Appeals for Veterans Claims would be left off those weekly notices. As of October 6, 2026, a House committee had approved it and it was placed on the House calendar for a vote.
for: Supporters say veterans often wait a long time with little information, and that knowing why appeals are delayed or sent back, and where the line stands each week, helps both veterans and Congress hold the board accountable.
against: Critics say extra reporting and weekly postings take staff time away from deciding cases, and that docket notices could raise false hopes because an assigned case may not be decided that week.
